why: Disjoint adjacent swaps work like tiling a line with monominoes (keep arr[i] in place) and dominoes (swap arr[i-1] with arr[i]). This is the classic 1-D DP: dp[i] = max(dp[i-1] + arr[i-1]*i, dp[i-2] + arr[i-2]*i + arr[i-1]*(i-1)).
hints: Because swaps cannot share an index, each element either stays put or trades places with exactly one neighbour.
Look at the last position: either element i stays (from dp[i-1]) or elements i-1 and i swapped (from dp[i-2]). That is the same structure as climbing stairs or domino tiling.
Run the recurrence with two rolling variables. O(n) time, O(1) space.
pitfalls: Values can be negative, so swapping is not always good. Let the max decide.
Positions are 1-based multipliers: element at index i is weighted i+1.
Results reach about 8000^2 * 1e9 / 2, beyond 32-bit (return type long).
